reason: I'll start with the lower body and place the digestive tract in its indicated space.

alternatives.reason: Attaching the arm to the chest also makes sense, but either region can come first.

reaction: It is satisfying to see the gut positioned with the liver and colon.
reason: I'll finish the lower body by fitting the urinary organs into their indicated space.
expectation: The kidneys, ureters and bladder should fit alongside the digestive tract.

effect: The lower body now has both organ groups, so I can move on to the chest.
reaction: The separate digestive and urinary outlets make their positions clearer.

expectation: The arm assembly should connect at the shoulder, while the lymph connection remains to be fitted.

alternatives.reason: The lymph network also belongs at the chest, but I chose to attach the arm first.

effect: The arm is attached, including its blood and nerve connections; the lymph network still needs fitting.
reaction: It is useful to see how the arm connects to the rest of the body.
reason: I'll connect the lymph drainage network to the chest; it's the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The lymph vessels should connect to the neck vein, completing the chest goal.

effect: The lymph network is connected at the existing vein, and the chest and lower body are ready to join.
reaction: The shared vein connection makes the assembly clearer.
reason: I'll join the two completed regions; it's the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The chest should fit above the lower body, connecting their existing routes.

effect: The chest and lower body are joined, and the open back channel shows where the spine belongs.
reaction: Seeing the diaphragm separate the organs while routes cross it makes the layout clearer.
reason: I'll join the head and spine to the trunk; it's the only offered gameplay action and matches the new goal.
expectation: The spine should fit into the back channel, connecting the head and nerve routes to the trunk.

effect: The head and spine are joined to the trunk, leaving the skin covering to fit.
reaction: Seeing nerves and blood routes reach the same muscles ties the earlier builds together.
reason: I'll fit the skin covering last, as instructed; it's the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The covering should fit over the assembled body, with the repaired segment at its original forearm location.

effect: The covering completes the body while the cutaway keeps the connected organs visible; all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The scar staying in its original place is a satisfying reminder that this is the same model.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the chest and lower body was most worthwhile: the diaphragm and the separate routes crossing between regions made the overall layout clearer.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the lymph network was less engaging as an assembly step: it mainly aligned a connection that was already built.

surprise.text: The final cutaway showed replacement cells still being made, reminding me that the completed body is not just a collection of fixed parts.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the later choices were mostly single offered actions rather than decisions I had to figure out.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter explored how the assembled systems work together; that connection was more interesting than simply fitting the remaining pieces.
